p.i: ὁ μακάριος ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν ὑπαρχόντα, &c.

main_text.p: 2. Vt nec solis naturę uiribus, nec etiam casu bona naturalia & alia commoda huius uitæ sparguntur, sed prouidentia diuina κατὰ μέτρον omnia dispensantur: sic ea miscentur & temperantur malis & incommodis quibusdam, quæ etiam nō sunt αὐτὸν τινὸς συγγνώμης.

Humanarum rerum necessariū quod-dam temperamentum esse, consensus omnium intelligentium, & experientia uni-uersalis testantur. Est enim hominum generi luctandum & laborandum inter uitam & mortem, spem & metum, bona & mala, commoda & incommoda, uelut inter contrarios fluctus.Diuinitus autem ita comparatum esse, quis sanus, finem rerum istarum intuens, non uideat? Res secundæ animum addunt, spem fouent, mitigant sensum dolorum quem aduersa pariunt. Hæc autem modestos & cautos efficiunt. Dona Dei, quæ parturiente rerum natura nobis subministrantur, uelut large Dei manu percipere oportet cum gratiarum actione: non autem partim naturæ uiribus, partim nostris meritis accepta ferre.

page.notes: The opening Greek line is printed in italic and is partly blurred; the letters are copied as far as legible. The Greek phrases "κατὰ μέτρον" and "αὐτὸν τινὸς συγγνώμης" are uncertain at the end of the second. The section sign before "Nec" is read as §; its shape is unclear. The line break after "fluctus." has no space in print ("fluctus.Diuinitus"), kept as printed. Long s has been written as plain s throughout.
